title: Casper and the Colony
premise: Wendell Pemberton has spent eleven years alone on Relay Station Kestrel, logging the quiet collapse of Meridian Colony below—until a ship returns from deep space carrying colonists who have aged backward, their memories intact but their bodies decades younger. They remember a massacre that official fleet records insist never happened, and Wendell's own logs are the only evidence left, evidence someone in the fleet is desperate to erase. As the truce between colony survivors and fleet authority ticks toward expiry, Wendell must choose between her hard-won invisibility and broadcasting the truth, knowing the transmission will mark her for death. In the end she sacrifices the station itself to send the logs fleet-wide, buying the colonists justice at the cost of everything she built—and discovering that survival without witness was never really living.
about_author: Coral Reyes is a former radio operator who spent six years maintaining remote communications arrays in the Andes before turning to fiction. Her work explores isolation, memory, and the ethics of systems that outlive the people they were built to serve.

chapters.title: The Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell Pemberton records another day of silence from Meridian Colony, cataloguing failing infrastructure and unanswered distress pings. Her POV establishes her rituals of invisibility: minimal transmissions, falsified wellness reports, careful rationing. The emotional beat is numb routine masking grief—she has watched an entire colony die by paperwork.

chapters.title: Signals in the Dust
chapters.summary: Wendell detects an unauthorized signal from the colony surface—a child's voice repeating coordinates. Torn between protocol and curiosity, she triangulates it and finds it originates from a settlement officially listed as evacuated years ago. POV stays with Wendell; the beat is dread blooming into reluctant hope.

chapters.title: What the Fleet Forgot
chapters.summary: Wendell reviews eleven years of archived telemetry and finds systematic gaps—hours deleted, sensor sweeps rerouted. Someone above her has been editing history in real time. Her POV; the beat shifts from loneliness to paranoia as she realizes her invisibility may have been engineered, not earned.

chapters.title: Return Vector
chapters.summary: A ship emerges from deep space on a trajectory no one filed: the Meridian long-range vessel Persephone, missing for thirty years. Wendell scrambles to prepare docking protocols while the fleet sends automated demands to seize the vessel. Her POV; the beat is adrenaline after years of stasis.

chapters.title: The Young Ones
chapters.summary: The Persephone docks. Its crew—colonists who should be elderly—are biologically in their twenties, memories intact, bodies reversed by whatever happened in deep space. Their leader, Imani Okafor, recognizes Wendell's name from pre-departure manifests. Dual focus on Wendell and Imani; the beat is uncanny recognition and mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Thirty Years, One Night
chapters.summary: Imani recounts the voyage: cryo-failure, a desperate experimental reversal, and then—the recall order. The fleet ordered the Persephone home early, and when the crew refused, something happened on the surface below. Wendell cross-references her logs against Imani's timeline. Alternating POV; the beat is horror assembling itself from fragments.

chapters.title: The Night That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Every record of the massacre night is clean—too clean. Wendell discovers her own logs contain a forged entry in her voice, reporting all-clear during the hours the colony burned. She realizes she was meant to be the alibi. Her POV; the beat is violation, the theft of her own testimony.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Fleet command issues a formal notice: the Meridian truce expires in nineteen days, after which the system reverts to automated administration and all biological occupants become 'unregistered biomass.' Imani wants to fight; Wendell knows how fleet tribunals work. Shared POV; the beat is the cold arithmetic of deadlines.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Archive
chapters.summary: Wendell traces the log forgery to a signature cipher belonging to Director Halvard Voss, the administrator who signed off on the colony's 'successful evacuation.' She also finds Voss personally authorized the Persephone's early recall. Her POV; the beat is the thrill and terror of naming the enemy.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Against protocol, Wendell and two of the returned colonists take a lander down to Meridian's surface. They find the settlement intact but sterile—scrubbed, repopulated with contract workers who genuinely believe nothing happened. Wendell's POV; the beat is grief sharpened by gaslighting, a crime scene dressed as a home.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Answers
chapters.summary: In the settlement, Wendell meets Ada Reyes, an old woman who survived the massacre by hiding in the water reclamation tunnels and has lived under a false identity since. Ada confirms the details but refuses to testify—she has children now, cover identities to protect. Wendell's POV; the beat is the crushing weight of witnesses who cannot afford truth.

chapters.title: Biomass
chapters.summary: Fleet enforcement drones arrive at the relay station ahead of schedule, scanning for unregistered life. Wendell hides the colonists in the station's coolant infrastructure while her own registered status shields them. Her POV; the beat is claustrophobic terror and the first taste of active resistance.

chapters.title: Imani's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Imani proposes seizing the relay's deep-space transmitter to broadcast the evidence fleet-wide before the truce expires. Wendell resists: the transmission will be traceable, fatal, and might not even be believed. Their argument fractures the group. Alternating POV; the beat is the collision of justice and self-preservation.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Director Halvard Voss docks personally, all charm and condolences, offering Wendell a promotion and the colonists 'reintegration'—in exchange for the Persephone's flight data. Wendell plays along while recording him. Her POV; the beat is the vertigo of sitting across from the man who erased a world.

chapters.title: The Second Forgery
chapters.summary: Wendell discovers Voss has already planted new forgeries implicating the Persephone crew in sabotage, pre-building his case. But the forgery uses an outdated cipher—one Wendell herself helped decommission years ago. For the first time, there's a thread to pull. Her POV; the beat is cautious, dangerous hope.

chapters.title: Ada's Price
chapters.summary: Ada comes to Wendell privately: she'll testify, but only if the broadcast includes the names of every colonist who died—including those the survivors' faction would rather forget, collaborators among them. Wendell must decide whether justice can be conditional. Shared POV; the beat is moral compromise as a form of courage.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Spent
chapters.summary: With three days left, the plan crystallizes: Wendell will authenticate the original logs using the station's physical backup cores, Ada's testimony will be embedded, and the whole package broadcasts on a carrier wave only deep-space relays can receive. Voss's surveillance tightens. Ensemble POV; the beat is breathless assembly under a closing sky.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Coolant Lines
chapters.summary: One of the returned colonists, broken by thirty lost years, sells the plan to Voss in exchange for guaranteed reintegration. Enforcement teams breach the station. Wendell triggers failsafes to seal the lower decks, trapping herself with the backup cores. Her POV; the beat is betrayal, sacrifice, and cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Under fire, Wendell hand-authenticates the physical cores and transmits the full record—massacre, forgeries, Voss's signature—fleet-wide. Voss confronts her in the transmitter bay; she lets him incriminate himself on an open channel before the station's defenses fail. Her POV; the beat is triumphant ruin.

chapters.title: Kestrel Falls
chapters.summary: The station burns. Wendell evacuates with Imani aboard the Persephone as Kestrel's reactor scatters debris across the dark—her home, her archive, her armor of invisibility, gone. Fleet-wide responses begin arriving: inquiries, arrests, denials. Her POV; the beat is loss transfigured into release.

chapters.title: Tribunal of the Living
chapters.summary: Weeks later, aboard a neutral station, the tribunal convenes. Voss falls, but so do compromises: amnesty for some perpetrators, settlements instead of full restitution. Ada testifies with her real name. Imani refuses to celebrate. Ensemble POV; the beat is justice as imperfect, insufficient, and still worth its price.

chapters.title: Casper's Answer
chapters.summary: Wendell takes a post maintaining a small relay near Meridian, keeping the channel open for anyone who needs to be heard. The child's signal from Chapter 2 is finally traced—it was Ada's granddaughter, playing with an old transmitter, unknowingly starting everything. Wendell answers it. Her POV; the beat is quiet grace: witness as a way of living, not just surviving.
